title: Race, Ethnicity and Their Implication on Bias in Large Language Models
benchmark_measurement: The study measures how religious identities (specifically Jewish and Muslim) are encoded within LLMs at the neuron level. It identifies neurons that represent religious concepts and associated stereotypes, often as a facet of the 'Middle Eastern' ethnic category, and analyzes how these internal representations are activated and influence model behavior.
findings: LLMs encode religious identities, such as Jewish and Muslim, into specific, interpretable neurons, often as part of a broader 'Middle Eastern' ethnic representation. These neurons project to religious identifiers (e.g., 'Jewish', 'Judaism', 'Islam', 'Jerusalem') and are selectively activated by related text. The paper demonstrates that these religious concepts are decomposed into distinct semantic facets within the model, and their presence suggests that bias mitigation requires model-specific localization rather than a universal approach.
